priorStories.headline: Lula wins fourth term in Brazil
priorStories.body:
Brazil’s electoral court declared President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reelected to a fourth nonconsecutive term. He received 51.79% of valid votes, compared with 48.21% for Flávio Bolsonaro.

Bolsonaro refused to concede and said he would seek to annul the result because voting was extended at polling places that remained open late. The electoral court’s president said the extension did not affect the outcome.

priorStories.headline: Vucic concedes Serbia election to student movement
priorStories.body:
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in the country’s parliamentary election after preliminary sampling showed the student-led Students’ List had won.

The list was projected to take 135 to 140 of parliament’s 250 seats, enough for a majority. Final official results were still pending.

priorStories.headline: Zelenskyy says U.S. missile warnings restored
priorStories.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said U.S. warnings about imminent Russian ballistic-missile attacks had been fully restored after recent disruptions.

He also said SpaceX’s military-focused Starshield service had operated without its earlier speed restriction since Saturday morning. Zelenskyy attributed both changes to discussions with U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff.

candidates.summary: Jordanian security forces arrested three armed suspects sought after the October 23 attack on a Greek Orthodox church funeral in Karak that killed eight people. The Public Security Directorate said the suspects were found in an abandoned house in Al-Jadeeda on Monday, refused to surrender and were wounded in an exchange of fire before being taken into custody. No security personnel were reported hurt.
candidates.title: Jordan arrests three suspects after deadly church attack

candidates.summary: The Chinese Communist Party’s Central Committee began a four-day closed-door plenum focused on strengthening party discipline and governance. About 300 committee members were expected to discuss a draft policy decision on tighter internal oversight amid Xi Jinping’s continuing anticorruption campaign.
candidates.title: Chinese Communist Party begins discipline-focused plenum

candidates.summary: The Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognized government carried out airstrikes on Houthi-held territory, including the capital, Sanaa, according to live reporting. The strikes came amid renewed fighting between the coalition and the Iran-aligned Houthi movement.
candidates.title: Saudi-led coalition carries out airstrikes in Sanaa

candidates.summary: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said they attacked Saudi Arabia’s East-West crude-oil pumping stations and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed the claimed attacks. The announcement came as the Saudi-led coalition said it had destroyed Houthi ballistic-missile launchers in Sanaa, including one allegedly used to fire an intercepted missile toward Riyadh.
candidates.title: Houthis claim attacks on Saudi oil stations and Riyadh airport

candidates.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said his government would announce measures responding to weeks of protests over education, living costs and other grievances. Macron did not detail the package. He and Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said further unrest was expected during demonstrations planned for October 31.
candidates.title: Macron promises measures in response to French protests

candidates.summary: Six U.S. citizens filed a federal lawsuit in New York challenging President Donald Trump’s policy of expelling reporters from White House premises. The plaintiffs argue that excluding news organizations infringes the public’s right to receive independent reporting about the president and federal government. The defendants include Trump and three aides, including White House chief of staff Susie Wiles.
candidates.title: Citizens sue over White House expulsions of reporters

The announcement did not specify the number of troops or a deployment timetable.
candidates.title: Algeria orders military deployment to Niger

candidates.summary: Jordanian security forces arrested three Jordanian relatives after a shootout in Al-Jadeeda, identifying them as the gunmen in the October 23 attack on a Greek Orthodox church funeral in Karak. Jordan’s official news agency said the attack killed nine people and injured 34, correcting the previously reported death toll of eight. The suspects were wounded during their arrest; no security personnel were reported injured.
candidates.title: Jordan arrests three suspects after church attack that killed nine

candidates.summary: France’s government announced measures responding to protests over education and living costs, including replacing the Parcoursup university-admissions platform by 2028 and creating 15,000 additional higher-education places during 2027 and 2028. Other commitments included limits on some class sizes and financing for school renovations. The replacement admissions system still must be designed and may require legislation.
candidates.title: France announces education concessions after mass protests

sources.name: French Ministry of Higher Education and Research

candidates.summary: Jordan said it carried out airstrikes against armed groups in southern Syria that it linked to the October 23 church attack in Karak. Jordan said militants were killed or wounded but did not identify the groups or disclose strike locations. Syria said seven civilians were killed in Daraa and Sweida, including three children, and said Jordan had not coordinated the operation. Syria subsequently closed its main border crossing with Jordan.
candidates.title: Jordan strikes Syria over deadly Karak church attack

candidates.summary: Egypt’s House of Representatives authorized President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi to provide military support to Saudi Arabia if requested, following escalating Houthi attacks on the kingdom. Egyptian officials described the mandate as defensive and said it would not include attacks inside Yemen. The authorization clears the constitutional requirement for a possible deployment but does not itself confirm that Egyptian forces have been sent.
candidates.title: Egypt authorizes defensive military support for Saudi Arabia

candidates.summary: Anthropic filed a Form S-1 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a proposed initial public offering. The company said it intends to list Class A shares on Nasdaq under the symbol ANT. The number of shares and proposed price range have not been determined, and the registration statement has not yet taken effect.
candidates.title: Anthropic publicly files for proposed IPO

candidates.summary: The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church’s Holy Synod said 60 Orthodox Christians were killed and more than 20 seriously injured in attacks in Oromia’s Arsi Zone on October 20 and October 24. The church attributed 14 deaths to an attack in Merti district and 46 to attacks in Shirka district. It called for government protection and prosecution of those responsible. Independent reporting cited differing casualty estimates, and the perpetrators had not been publicly established.
candidates.title: Ethiopian church reports 60 killed in Oromia attacks

candidates.summary: Court documents unsealed Monday revealed that the U.S. Justice Department had filed a criminal information against former FBI Director James Comey alleging two felony counts related to the disclosure of classified information in 2016. The filing was submitted under seal on October 5 without a grand-jury indictment. Comey denies wrongdoing, and his lawyers asked the court to dismiss the case as legally invalid and outside the applicable limitations period.
candidates.title: Unsealed filings reveal new Justice Department case against Comey

candidates.summary: A federal judge ruled that the Justice Department unlawfully fired former federal prosecutor Maurene Comey. The judge ordered retroactive reinstatement and back pay from her dismissal through December 20, 2025, when she began private-sector employment. The ruling did not decide Comey’s separate claim that the firing violated her free-speech rights.
candidates.title: Judge rules Justice Department unlawfully fired Maurene Comey
